correctness.rationale: Checked that every antiprism edge belongs to an edge-overlap-connected family of triangles; an adjacent selected pair forces its triangle and then every triangle, yielding the full set. Distance-two selected pairs force the middle vertex, so no proper convex subset can have pairs within distance two. Conversely any distance-two packing meets the outside-neighbor rule. Each selected cyclic column has A or B, with successive gaps >=2 and a gap 2 allowed only from A to B; both directed gaps are checked even for two sites and n=3. The weighted 2x2 transfer R=t²E+t³J/(1-t) produces the labelled cyclic enumeration -t d/dt log det(I-zR), yielding the claimed rational GF; nonconsecutive short gaps prove floor(2n/5) and explicit constructions attain it. Fresh independently implemented outside-neighbor subset enumeration for n=3..9 agrees exactly with independent distance-two packing enumeration and rational coefficients. Finite checking supports the proof, which is symbolic for all n.

value.rationale: Antiprism graphs are a natural vertex-transitive 4-regular planar family. The theorem gives a structural closure classification and complete graded convexity polynomial, with a sharp packing threshold, beyond a finite small-graph census.

final_claim: For every n>=3, P3-convex subsets of antiprism A_n are precisely the empty set, whole graph, and nonempty graph-distance>=3 packings. Their cardinality polynomial satisfies sum_{n>=3}(C_n(z)-1-z^(2n))t^n = (2zt^3(3-2t)+z^2t^5(5-4t))/((1-t)(1-t-2zt^3-z^2t^5)); maximum size of a proper convex subset is floor(2n/5).
limitations: Applies to labelled vertex subsets of n-gonal antiprisms n>=3, not automorphism orbit counts or arbitrary planar 4-regular graphs.
An earlier independence-polynomial formula for the square of antiprism graph, perhaps under circulant/Cayley terminology, would imply the claimed generating function.
Direct subset computation is bounded n<=9, while all-n claim relies on triangle propagation and transfer matrix proof.
